property_summary: After ownership is transferred to any address and that owner calls NETM(), the owner's token balance must equal totalDistributed; the mutant assigns totalRemaining instead, so balances diverge whenever totalDistributed != totalRemaining (always, since totalSupply = 2*totalDistributed).

Only the contract owner's NETM() call can mint the totalDistributed stash: for any caller, calling NETM() must leave that caller's balanceOf unchanged; the mutant lets any caller claim balances[caller] == totalDistributed, breaking the invariant.

property_summary: For any caller and any address k, a failed NETM call leaves every balance untouched: since only the deployer/owner may call NETM in P (any non-owner call reverts, so c.balanceOf(k) stays 0 for all k), while in M any caller mints totalDistributed to themselves, so choosing k = caller yields c.balanceOf(k) == totalDistributed and breaks the rule.

For any non-owner caller and any address k, calling NETM() must leave c.balanceOf(k) at its pre-call value (0), because only the owner may execute NETM; the mutant lets any caller mint totalDistributed to itself, so balanceOf(k) becomes nonzero, violating the rule.

After ownership has been transferred to a fuzzed newOwner, any caller different from newOwner must have its NETM() call revert (only the current owner may execute it), but the mutant lets any caller execute it and mint totalDistributed to itself.
